finding.claim: LRUCache.set deletes an existing key and then fails to re-insert it, so updating any cached key loses the entry.
finding.title: LRUCache.set drops updates to existing keys

verifier.reason: The code at internal/lrucache.js:26-35 deletes the key first and only calls this.map.set inside if (!deleted && value !== undefined), so setting an existing key with a defined value deletes it without re-inserting it.

repro.testCode:
import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
import LRUCache from './internal/lrucache.js'

const cache = new LRUCache()
cache.set('key', 'first')
assert.equal(cache.get('key'), 'first')
cache.set('key', 'second')
assert.equal(cache.get('key'), 'second')
assert.equal(cache.map.size, 1)
cache.set('other', 1)
cache.set('other', 2)
assert.equal(cache.get('other'), 2)
assert.equal(cache.get('key'), 'second')
repro.expectedBehavior: LRUCache.set on an existing key updates its value and retains the entry, so a subsequent get returns the new value.
repro.rationale: The buggy set() only inserts when delete() returned false, so updating an existing key deletes it without re-inserting. Setting a key twice and asserting get returns the updated value fails on the buggy code (undefined) and passes when fixed.
